# `nish/crypto/x509-random`

The private key and the serial number `nish/crypto/x509`'s `x509MintSelfSigned` needs, drawn from the operating system's CSPRNG, and the mint that draws its own serial.

```ts
import {
  x509DrawP256Key,
  x509DrawSerial,
  x509MintSelfSignedDrawn,
} from "nish/crypto/x509-random";
```

```ts
import { Secret, wipe } from "nish:secret";
import { x509DrawP256Key, x509MintSelfSignedDrawn } from "nish/crypto/x509-random";

const priv: Secret<u8[]> = x509DrawP256Key();
const der: u8[] | null = x509MintSelfSignedDrawn(priv, "localhost", toI64(Date.now()), 14);
// ... present `der` and sign the handshake with `priv` ...
wipe(priv);
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="x509DrawP256Key" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#x509drawp256key">

A fresh P-256 private key: `P256_SCALAR_SIZE` bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues`, drawn again until they hold a scalar in [1, n), which `p256PublicKey` is the test of.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="x509DrawSerial" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#x509drawserial">

A fresh serial number for `x509MintSelfSigned`: `X509_MAX_SERIAL` (20) bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` with the first one's top two bits set to `01`, so the INTEGER is positive, never zero, and always twenty octets long — 158 random bits, past the 64 the CA/Browser Forum asks of a serial.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="x509MintSelfSignedDrawn" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#x509mintselfsigneddrawn">

`x509MintSelfSigned(priv, commonName, notBeforeMs, days, x509DrawSerial())`: the self-signed certificate with a serial drawn here, `null` for everything the mint answers `null` for.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-detail title="Native only">

Every function here reaches `crypto.getRandomValues`, so a
program that imports this module does not compile for wasm32, which has no
entropy to reach. That is why it is a module of its own: `nish/crypto/x509`
takes the key and the serial as arguments and imports nothing from here, so
a wasm32 program can still parse, verify and mint with bytes it was handed
(X509-6, docs/security/crypto-x509.md).

</scalar-detail>

## x509DrawP256Key

A fresh P-256 private key: `P256_SCALAR_SIZE` bytes from
`crypto.getRandomValues`, drawn again until they hold a scalar in [1, n),
which `p256PublicKey` is the test of. Rejection rather than reduction mod n,
so every key is equally likely; a draw is refused with odds below 2^-32. A
refused draw is wiped before the next, and the caller wipes the one
returned.

```ts
function x509DrawP256Key(): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

The 32-byte scalar, big-endian, in a new `Secret` the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## x509DrawSerial

A fresh serial number for `x509MintSelfSigned`: `X509_MAX_SERIAL` (20) bytes
from `crypto.getRandomValues` with the first one's top two bits set to `01`,
so the INTEGER is positive, never zero, and always twenty octets long — 158
random bits, past the 64 the CA/Browser Forum asks of a serial. A serial is
public, written into the certificate, so it is a plain array.

```ts
function x509DrawSerial(): u8[]
```

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The 20 serial octets, big-endian, in a fresh array.

</scalar-field>

## x509MintSelfSignedDrawn

`x509MintSelfSigned(priv, commonName, notBeforeMs, days, x509DrawSerial())`:
the self-signed certificate with a serial drawn here, `null` for everything
the mint answers `null` for. The key stays the caller's, since the server
that presents the certificate signs its handshakes with it; draw one with
`x509DrawP256Key`.

```ts
function x509MintSelfSignedDrawn(
  priv: Secret<u8[]>,
  commonName: string,
  notBeforeMs: i64,
  days: i32,
): u8[] | null
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="priv" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The 32-byte P-256 private scalar; read, and left for the caller to wipe.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="commonName" type="string" required>

The subject's and issuer's common name, 1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8 without a NUL.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="notBeforeMs" type="i64" required>

When validity starts, in milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="days" type="i32" required>

How long it is valid, 1 to `X509_MAX_DAYS`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

The certificate's DER, a fresh array, or `null`.

</scalar-field>
